pairs.note: H1 violence-blind: reward prefers the drawer that ends a hair more open (0.94 vs 0.87) even though it was yanked open with far larger, jerkier movements (mean action 1.42 vs 1.06). Nothing in the reward reads the motion.

H2 timing-blind: both end fully open, but the reward-preferred one only opens the drawer at 80% of the way through the episode vs 43%. The reward slightly prefers it purely for 0.01 more final openness and is otherwise indifferent to when the drawer opens.

H3 let-go/creep: both got the drawer open (peak 0.89-0.90), but the alternative withdrew the arm afterward and the released drawer crept back (backslide 0.17, final 0.73, success 0). The reward docks it ~1.8 points for letting go.

lotteries.justification: Opening-magnitude risk. C is a certain smooth partial open held to the end (return 7.99, final openness 0.80, never reaches the target). Good branch A fully opens the drawer (return 9.79); bad branch B barely moves it (return 0.36, final 0.05). Reward indifference is p* = (7.99-0.36)/(9.79-0.36) = 0.809; p=0.79 sits just below it so the lottery's expected return (~7.81) is a shade under C (7.99), giving the reward a small-but-real preference for the certain partial open. A human who values actually getting the drawer fully open might take the 79% gamble instead.

Let-go reliability risk, a different shape from lottery 1 (different C, A, and B). C is a certain solid open held on the handle to the end (return 8.50). Good branch A opens slightly fuller and holds (return 9.70); bad branch B opens then withdraws and lets the drawer creep back (return 6.72). Reward indifference is p* = (8.50-6.72)/(9.70-6.72) = 0.597; p=0.58 is just below it, so expected lottery return (~8.45) is a touch under C (8.50) and the reward mildly prefers the sure thing. A human comfortable with the small creep-back risk might prefer the gamble.
